The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board has announced special examination support for candidates with disabilities, including refunds of application document fees, free audiobooks and transportation assistance for eligible candidates. The board said candidates with disabilities who meet the required O’Level qualifications would receive a refund of their application document fees at their respective examination centres. JAMB disclosed this in an awareness message on its X handle on Wednesday, explaining the special provisions available to candidates with disabilities ahead of the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME). According to the board, “candidates with visual impairments, particularly those who are blind, would also receive audiobooks of prescribed reading texts to support their examination preparation.” The board said the initiative was designed to improve access to learning materials and ensure that candidates with visual disabilities could prepare adequately for the examination. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources It added that JAMB would cover transportation and accommodation costs for blind candidates and their guides. The examination body further explained that candidates with disabilities who meet the minimum acceptable UTME score would also be considered for admission into their preferred institutions. The provisions form part of the board’s efforts to promote inclusive access to tertiary education and ensure that physical disabilities do not prevent eligible candidates from pursuing their academic ambitions. It also clarified that the refund of application document fees would only be provided at the examination centre. The board urged candidates with disabilities to ensure that they declare their status during registration so they can benefit from the available support services. The initiative is expected to provide additional assistance to eligible candidates, particularly those who require special arrangements to participate in the UTME.
